findings.title: Shared randomness across recipients plus unauthenticated recipient keys: a rogue key makes M public with no secret key at all
findings.detail: 1.2 wraps every recipient with one r: c_i = M + r*A_i. Any known linear relation sum(lambda_i*A_i) = O with sum(lambda_i) != 0 yields sum(lambda_i*c_i) = sum(lambda_i)*M. Concrete: register an identity whose EndpointId encodes -A_alice (iroh PublicKey::from_bytes == VerifyingKey::from_bytes accepts it; AddIdentity takes hex with no proof of possession; the point is canonical, torsion-free and distinct from A_alice, so V6 passes) and get it granted read through normal onboarding; or in mode B a group admin adds the row directly, since V5 never requires registration. Then M = (c_alice + c_rogue)*inv(2) from the record bytes alone; 2*A_alice gives M = 2*c_alice - c_rogue; A_a + A_b gives M = c_a + c_b - c_x. The DLEQ statement is true, so the proof verifies. Verified numerically against curve25519-dalek 5. Consequences: a stolen SQLite file (records + ciphertext) is readable with no key, contradicting the threat model; the authoritative node reads a mode-B group; the 'no hidden recipient' claim of 1.5 is false; the rogue ACL row looks like an ordinary identity and nobody holds its secret key. Today's age wraps use a per-stanza ephemeral share, so this weakness is introduced by the design; randomness reuse in multi-recipient ElGamal is only secure for independently generated keys.
findings.fix: Use independent randomness per recipient: c0_i = r_i*B, c_i = M + r_i*A_i (wrap entry pk || c0_i || c_i, 96 B). Prove knowledge of (r_1..r_n) with c0_i = r_i*B for all i and c_i - c_1 = r_i*A_i - r_1*A_1 for i >= 2: one Fiat-Shamir challenge, n responses (proof 32 + 32n bytes). Verified numerically that the rogue-key combination then fails. Alternative keeping shared r: each reader key carries a self-signature over (genesis, endpoint id) in the first epoch that wraps to it (PoP replicas can verify) - but it cannot cover the X25519 pinned keys and needs the reader online at grant time, so prefer per-recipient r_i. In both variants also reject identity/small-order recipients (see finding 4).

findings.title: Server-authored minting epochs are legal on end-to-end chains, so a hostile authoritative node can put a key it knows at the head (invisibly, or by pinning itself)
findings.detail: V9(c) admits a server-authored keys epoch with ACL == prev.acl, 'only pinned changed', and 'mint may be true or false'; V9(a) admits a server-authored genesis; V8 lets only server-authored epochs change pinned. On a mode-B group the server mints M', wraps to readers ∪ pinned with a valid proof (it knows r'), sets dek_version = head+1, and stages whatever it likes (nobody checks re-encryption content in mode B; if it leaves old rows untouched replicas do not refetch them because (current_version, dek_version, nonce) is unchanged). The head generation is now one the server holds; PutSealed must use the head generation (DekConflict otherwise), so every future write is server-readable while readers see nothing broken. Variant: pinned += operational, a visible B->A downgrade admins cannot revert because V8 forbids admin-authored pinned changes. Same for migration/CreateGroup into dek_mode = e2e: the server minted M at epoch 1 and knows it until an admin mints, yet nothing sets needs_rotation or refuses sealed writes. Contradicts 5.5 ('a hostile authoritative node cannot add a reader on a mode-B group').
findings.fix: On a chain whose prev.pinned lacks operational, restrict server-authored epochs to genesis, removal-only carry, and keys with mint == false (re-pin/recover with commit == head.commit); never a mint. Adding operational to pinned requires an admin author holding read (allow an admin-authored pinned change only inside a mint that adds operational, surfaced as a mode change). Mode-B clients treat a server-minted head generation (genesis included) as needs_rotation and refuse PutSealed until an admin mints; replicas emit EpochRejected on any server-authored mint on a sealed chain. Document that a mode-B group is end-to-end only from the first admin-authored mint onward.

findings.title: carry can move the head generation backwards and re-add wraps without M: V7 checks carry.dek_version against the referenced epoch, not the head
findings.detail: V6 allows carry.from to be any earlier keys epoch; V7 requires only dek_version == epoch[from].dek_version. Chain: e10 keys gen 8 wraps {alice, bob, backup}; e11 alice mints gen 9 minus bob and re-encrypts. The server (V9(b) removal-only carry) or any admin authors e12 = carry{from:10, removed:[bob]}, acl == e11.acl, dek_version 8, mint false. V6: wraps(10) - {bob} == readers(e11.acl) ∪ pinned. V7: 8 == epoch[10].dek_version. V9(b): no additions. Head generation is now 8, the key bob holds; Put (mode A, 'DEK from the head record's operational wrap') and PutSealed (head generation) encrypt every subsequent write under it; replicas accept because the epoch-10 wrap opens for them. The kick is silently undone by an epoch that verifies. Variant: a write/admin-only admin (no M) carries from e10 with removed = [] and an ACL that re-adds bob's read bit - 'adding a reader requires M' (3.1) is false, and after a mode-B tombstone the now-unregistered id is re-added and R1 synthesizes an identity for it on replicas. Also 'commit == prev_keys.commit' in V7 is undefined once carry can point past the last mint.
findings.fix: Track explicit head state per chain: (dek_version, commit, effective wrap set, mint epoch). Every non-mint epoch: dek_version == prev.dek_version. Mint: dek_version > prev.dek_version and a never-seen commit. Carry may only shrink: effective(new) = effective(prev) - removed with removed ⊆ effective(prev); carry.from must reference the newest keys epoch of the current generation. Keys with mint == false: commit == head.commit and wrap set ⊇ effective(prev) restricted to the new ACL (adds only).

findings.title: The identity element is never excluded: c0 = O (r = 0) and identity-point recipients pass every rule and publish M
findings.detail: is_torsion_free(O) is true (verified) and no rule says c0 != O or A_i != O. With r = 0: c0 = O, every c_i = M; proof k random, T_0 = k*B, T_i = k*(A_i - A_1), s = k; verifier T_0' = e*O + k*B, T_i' = k*(A_i - A_1) + e*(c_i - c_1) = k*(A_i - A_1) since c_i - c_1 = O; e' == e. Anyone holding the record derives the DEK; a malicious admin makes a group world-readable while the chain shows a clean kick, and in mode B the server reads it. Independently, a recipient A_x = O (EndpointId 0x01 00..00 parses via VerifyingKey::from_bytes; the AddIdentity torsion check passes; V6 passes) gives c_x = M directly, and this survives the per-recipient-randomness fix of finding 1. A small-order A_x leaks M up to 8 candidates resolved by KCV, caught only if the torsion check runs in V6 as well as AddIdentity. Also iroh's PublicKey stores compressed bytes as received, so a non-canonical hex id can be registered today and then never be a recipient (V6 rejects), wedging every group that grants it read.
findings.fix: Verifier: reject c0 == O, any A_i == O, any pinned point == O, and A_i - A_1 == O explicitly. AddIdentity: require canonical encoding, torsion-free, not identity. Reader side: reject a recovered M == O. Add all to the V1-V11 negative matrix and golden vectors.

findings.title: Pinned keys are not checked against the node's configured backup/operational public keys, and V8 then freezes whatever genesis says
findings.detail: A mode-B genesis is client-authored (SubmitEpoch with epoch == 1 by a service admin). Section 8's submission checks compare author, registration, staged digest and (mode A) KCV, never pinned.backup against meta.backup_pubkey. The author pins a key it holds under the 'backup' role; V8 forces every later epoch to copy it and forbids admin-authored changes, so group admins can never remove it; the real offline backup key cannot recover that group; the pinned key is a permanent recipient outside the ACL. Where the backup key is held by a different party than the service admin this is a covert reader; in every case it silently breaks disaster recovery for the group.
findings.fix: At every SubmitEpoch and every server-authored epoch enforce pinned.backup == to_edwards(meta.backup_pubkey) and, when present, pinned.operational == to_edwards(meta.operational_pubkey). Replicas stamp the backup point on first sight (TOFU, next to genesis) and reject any change to it that is not server-authored; epoch log prints pinned keys.

findings.title: A mint does not have to be fresh: exact reuse of an earlier M passes verification
findings.detail: For mint == true V7 only requires dek_version > prev.dek_version; nothing constrains commit. An admin 'kicks' bob with M_new = M_old: the KCV equals the earlier generation's commit (same salt for non-genesis generations), the proof is valid, the record is accepted, and bob keeps opening the 'rotated' generation with the key he already holds. Deriving M_new from M_old in a guessable way (2*M_old) is undetectable and inherent, but exact reuse is free to catch and is what a lazy or coerced client would do.
findings.fix: V7: mint == true requires commit != commit of every earlier keys epoch in the chain. Mode A additionally: recovered M must differ from every cached generation.

findings.title: HKDF salt for the genesis generation is ambiguous, and the claimed cross-group DEK binding is absent for generation 1 of every migrated group
findings.detail: 1.2 defines salt = genesis hash, zero at epoch 1, without saying whether the salt belongs to the epoch or the generation. A keys epoch at epoch 2 re-wrapping the epoch-1 generation (add reader, mint == false) must reproduce the same DEK and commit; deriving the salt from the current epoch (genesis now known) gives the new reader a different DEK and V7's commit equality cannot hold, so gen-1 groups cannot gain readers without a mint. Read per-generation, the migration generation of every existing group is derived with a zero salt forever, so 'binding the salt to the group's genesis hash makes a DEK unusable across groups' is false where most secrets live (the AAD still binds, so not a break, but the doc's argument is wrong).
findings.fix: Add a random 32-byte salt field to the genesis body, chosen before hashing, stored in secret_group, used for every generation of the group; or drop genesis from the KDF and rely on the AAD. Define the salt as a per-group constant and pin it in golden vectors.

findings.title: Fiat-Shamir transcript omits prev, author and n; e/s canonicality is unspecified
findings.detail: Two forks with the same genesis (the authoritative restore/rewind R0' discusses) share epoch numbers, so a keys map proven for epoch n on the old fork verifies at epoch n on the new one. A write/admin-only admin without read copies alice's pre-restore (c0, wraps, proof, commit) into her own epoch n (ACLs match right after a restore), sets mint == true, stages garbage matching her reencrypted digest; the chain says she re-encrypted the group, it is unreadable, and she never held M. Binding the author also stops one admin from presenting another's proof as their own. n is implicit only because items are fixed-width. Nothing requires e and s to be canonical scalars: from_bytes_mod_order would accept s + l, making proof bytes malleable (harmless under the signature but breaks uniqueness and golden vectors).
findings.fix: Hash prev || author || n (u64) into the transcript. Parse e and s with Scalar::from_canonical_bytes and reject otherwise. Add a negative test for cross-fork replay.

findings.title: Prover randomness hygiene is unspecified; k or r reuse is a full break and the prover runs on arbitrary admin machines
findings.detail: Two proofs with the same k and different challenges give r = (s1 - s2)/(e2 - e1) mod l; r reveals M = c_i - r*A_i for every i from public data, i.e., the new DEK goes to the kicked reader. r reused across two mints gives c_i - c_i' = M - M', so a reader holding M (the kicked one) gets M'. Section 14 seeds m, r, k from a deterministic test RNG; that pattern must not reach production paths. curve25519-dalek 5's Scalar::random wants rand_core 0.10 while the crate pins rand 0.8 (the scratch probe hit exactly this), which invites an ad-hoc RNG shim.
findings.fix: Derive r and k as hedged deterministic scalars: HKDF-SHA512(ikm = author secret scalar bytes || 32 OsRng bytes, info = domain || transcript inputs so far) then from_bytes_mod_order_wide; zeroize k, r and buffers; test that two proofs of the same statement differ and that r differs across epochs.

findings.title: Nonce uniqueness of client-supplied re-encryptions is never checked; a nonce collision under one DEK leaks plaintext XOR and the Poly1305 key to anyone holding the ciphertexts
findings.detail: Staged SealedVersions come from the admin's client, which picks the 12-byte nonces. A client bug (constant nonce, RNG state duplicated across a fork, a retry re-sending a buffer for a different version) produces (dek_version, nonce) collisions within a group. Mode A trial decryption succeeds anyway; mode B checks nothing; the AAD does not prevent keystream reuse. A stolen database then yields P1 xor P2 and the tag key with no key material. The same applies to PutSealed writers.
findings.fix: Server rejects any staged set or PutSealed whose (dek_version, nonce) already exists in the group or repeats within the set (one indexed lookup per row). Optionally derive client nonces as HKDF(per-run key, name || version).

findings.title: Authorship and recipient-set rules are internally inconsistent: V4 genesis contradicts V9(a), and ACL rows need not be registered identities
findings.detail: V4 says a genesis author must be in admins(acl); V9(a) allows a server-authored genesis and the server is never in an ACL (migration and CreateGroup need exactly that). V5 never requires ACL endpoint ids to be registered: on the server step 7's 'INSERT rows from record.acl' cannot succeed for an unregistered id (group_acl.identity_id is a foreign key), so such records fail in the database rather than by rule, while R1 on replicas synthesizes an identity row for the same id and authorizes it. Combined with finding 1 this is how an admin introduces an arbitrary recipient point; even after that fix it lets a group admin onboard keys the service admin never registered, on replicas only.
findings.fix: V4: genesis author in admins(acl) or author == ctx.authoritative. Submission: every ACL endpoint id must exist in identity (else Failed) before verify. Replicas: deny ACL rows whose id has no roster entry instead of synthesizing a name.

findings.title: Verify-before-decrypt is load-bearing, not hygiene: clamping gives no cofactor protection in Edwards arithmetic, and the joint-key argument depends on the proof of knowledge
findings.detail: Verified: a clamped-then-reduced dalek Scalar times an 8-torsion point is not the identity, so a reader's clamped a_i does nothing against torsion in c0 (unlike the X25519 ladder). Any path that multiplies a_i by an unverified c0 (a Get fast path, cache warm-up from stored rows, a replica serving a partially verified group) is a small-subgroup oracle: with c0 = r*B + T the KCV passes iff a_i*T = O, leaking a_i mod 8. 1.5 says the Thormarker analysis 'applies unchanged', but that covers signing plus a hashed-DH KEM; here the decryption output is the raw linear a_i*c0, and what makes it safe is that signature and PoK of r are checked before any private-key multiplication. Constant-time and zeroization requirements are stated only for the DEK cache.
findings.fix: Enforce ordering in the type system: decrypt takes a Verified<Record> witness only epoch::verify can construct, on server, replica and CLI. State the argument as 'plaintext-aware via PoK of r, verified before decryption'. KCV comparison via subtle::ConstantTimeEq; prover scalar mults constant-time, verifier vartime only. Zeroize the Scalar from SigningKey::to_scalar(), the [u8;32] from iroh::SecretKey::to_bytes(), the bech32-decoded age secret bytes, M (EdwardsPoint implements Zeroize), PRK/DEK/KCV buffers, and k and r.

strengths: Storing and verifying the author's exact body bytes (no canonical CBOR) removes the re-serialization mismatch class; strict parsing with a version field is right.

Canonical-encoding (recompress and compare) plus is_torsion_free on c0, every c_i and every A_i is necessary and, as specified, correct: verified that a torsion component in c0 can be ground into a passing proof (e*T = O for e = 0 mod 8), so the check is what stops it.
Including epoch and genesis in the DLEQ transcript stops copying a keys map into a new epoch, which a hostile server or a keyless admin would otherwise do.
The batched single-response proof is a sound Schnorr proof for a group homomorphism; per-recipient proofs are not needed for soundness (they are needed for the randomness fix, a different reason).
Deriving DEK and KCV from one PRK under distinct HKDF labels means the published commit reveals nothing about the DEK under the PRF assumption.

verify_strict for record signatures, a distinct signature domain prefix that cannot collide with TLS CertificateVerify or pkarr signables, and signing over the record hash keep the endpoint key's uses separable.
Keeping secret_aad and dek_version untouched leaves existing ciphertext binding unaffected.
verdict: Not sound as specified for the guarantees section 5.5 claims. The Schnorr/DLEQ machinery and the encoding checks are fine, but one shared r across recipients turns any adversarially related or degenerate recipient key into a public disclosure of M (stolen-database and mode-B guarantees fail with no secret key involved, verified numerically), the V9 rules let a hostile authoritative node mint a generation it knows on an end-to-end chain, and the V7 carry rule lets a kick be rolled back by an epoch that verifies. Switch to per-recipient randomness with a vector Schnorr proof, forbid server-authored mints on sealed chains, make generation and effective wrap set monotone across non-mint epochs, reject the identity element everywhere, and pin the backup point at submission; with those five changes the design delivers what it claims and the remaining items are hardening.
